features.name: quant_sentence_share
features.definition: What proportion of sentences across the counter-argument comments contain a number, URL, or percentage?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads (malformed/missing -> null). Concatenate all comment strings; split each into sentences with a regex split on (?<=[.!?])\s+ and newlines, dropping empty/whitespace-only pieces. A sentence is quantitative if it matches r'\d|%|https?://|www\.' (digit characters, percent sign, or URL). Value = quantitative sentences / total sentences pooled across all comments. Empty list or zero sentences -> null. Purely mechanical on current text; no semantic filtering.

h0: quant_sentence_share has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view (delta).
h1: Higher quant_sentence_share is associated with a higher probability that the OP changed their view.
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP view change). Numbers/URLs/percentages are detected mechanically by regex; digits may include non-evidential numbers (list numbering, dates, quotes of OP). Sentence splitting is approximate. Comments are pooled across the row; list order carries no chronology. Raw text could contain delta-award announcements or outcome text (e.g., '!delta'), which are not removed. Association only, not causal.
